Today's focus was deploying and configuring EVM-side bridge contracts for 7 tokens on Sepolia, and preparing the faucet/stash bridging flow.

Key Decisions Made
WHFT over HFT for all tokens
After extensive discussion, decided to use WrappedHyperFungibleToken (lock-and-release model) for all 7 tokens instead of HyperFungibleToken (burn-and-mint). Reason: the goal is bridging in liquidity, not creating new tokens. This also means the same contracts and flow will work on mainnet with just address changes.
Mock ERC20s for all 7 tokens
Since WBTC, USDT, UNI, AAVE have no canonical Sepolia deployments, and for testing consistency, deployed mock ERC20s for all 7 tokens. Minted 1,000,000 of each to the deployer wallet.
Faucet Architecture
Decided on a stash-based faucet approach — bridge a large amount from Sepolia to a Polkadex stash once, faucet distributes from the stash on Polkadex (fast, no gas per user). Users who want to withdraw back to Sepolia bridge directly via the pallet-hft send extrinsic.
